clinical_claim.scope: Every customer IDAT runs through this card. It quantifies the patient's immune-class architectural state at the cellular level — immune-class A-score (with 95% CI propagated from IAMAtlas MCMC posteriors), 51-cell immune fanout (aggregated to 19 customer-facing pages), immune cellular age + immune age delta (inflammaging quantum), Mahalanobis distance against the n=601 pooled-HC hull, and the patient's personal Cosmic Microwave Methylome (8-panel Mollweide PNG). The immune card produces no disease verdict — instead it produces the universal first-pass measurement that downstream disease cards interpret in context, with engine-internal concordance flags surfaced from the Stage 8 disease signature matrix v1.7 consultation.
clinical_claim.what_this_card_reports_to_customer: Immune A-score with 95% measurement range, immune cellular age + immune age delta (inflammaging quantum), tier verdict on the 6-tier physics-derived scale (SUPPRESSED / NORMAL / ELEVATED / WARBURG_TRANSITION / SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED / BREACH), per-cell findings on the 19 customer-facing pages when individual cells depart significantly, bidirectional-pattern flag when relevant, the patient's personal Cosmic Microwave Methylome 8-panel Mollweide PNG, Mahalanobis distance with CI surfaced as 'overall departure from healthy is X SDs (range L–U).'
clinical_claim.what_this_card_does_NOT_report: No disease names in the customer report. No diagnostic verdicts. No specific clinical follow-up recommendations. Disease-specific concordance flags from the Stage 8 disease signature matrix consultation are ENGINE-INTERNAL — they feed downstream disease cards' interpretation, never appearing in the customer's immune readout.
clinical_claim.framework_lineage: IAMAtlas single Bayesian deconvolution. All pre-build atlas references (Xu-538, Loyfer, EpiSCORE, Salas, UniLIFE, Caggiano TIM, Reinius) were INGESTED at IAMAtlas BUILD time as published per-cell methylation data points, not queried at runtime. EDEAR runs its own MCMC chains against those data points with EDEAR's H_min anchors and 8-class architectural taxonomy producing the IAMAtlas. At patient runtime, the chain runs Stage 0 → 10 every time against the IAMAtlas posterior only.

framework_methodology_clarification: Astro-Genetics: EDEAR's chain methodology adapts proven astrophysics/cosmology tools (Planck CMB NILC needlet decomposition for Stage 2 cross-method gate, HEALPix sphere pixelization for Stage 4.6 personal Cosmic Microwave Methylome rendering, Mollweide projection for customer-facing visualization, virial-theorem-derived Mahaffey number for tier physics) to methylome architecture. The 1.07 Warburg-transition line and the 1.10 architectural-fidelity breach line are physics-defined inflection points, not statistical percentiles.

_grouping_rationale._doc_note: Bidirectional-discipline reasoning: cell types that could move in opposite directions in the same disease pattern get separate pages; cells that consistently move together can share a page or sub-section.
_grouping_rationale.naive_CD4_vs_naive_CD8: Separate pages required. Chronic HIV selectively depletes naive CD4 more than naive CD8 — opposite-direction pattern documented in clinical literature. CMV chronic infection drives differential CD8 vs CD4 dynamics. Grouping these would mask HIV-status and chronic-viral-infection signatures at the customer level.
_grouping_rationale.B_cells_vs_naive_B_vs_memory_B_vs_plasma: Separate pages for naive B, memory B, and plasma cells. In multiple myeloma, plasma cells expand clonally while general B cells and naive B cells stay normal or DOWN. In B-cell lymphomas (DLBCL, follicular), the opposite — general B-cell up, plasma stays normal. Naive B cells specifically elevate near solid-tumor diagnosis (VAL-095 aBnv at 0-2yr d=+0.44/+0.49). The general B_cells page covers the umbrella signal; subset pages cover lineage-stage-specific patterns.
_grouping_rationale.macrophages_vs_microglia_vs_kupffer: Separate pages for tissue-resident macrophage subtypes. Microglia (CNS-resident) elevate in neurodegeneration patterns (AD, MS, PD, ALS) while peripheral macrophages stay normal — opposite-direction. Kupffer cells (liver-resident) DEPLETE in HCC while peripheral macrophages infiltrating tumor (TAMs) elevate — opposite-direction in same customer. Different organ-system patterns, different disease drivers, must stay separate.
_grouping_rationale.memory_T_cells_combined_CD4_and_CD8: Single memory_T_cells page covering both CD4Tmem and CD8Tmem. Memory T cell pool dynamics (chronic-viral-infection-driven memory inflation, TEMRA accumulation, immunosenescence) generally affect CD4mem and CD8mem in the same direction. CMV-driven CD8mem expansion is the strongest exception, but CD4mem typically also expands in CMV+ customers (just less dramatically). Treated as one page with sub-section discussion of subtype-specific findings.

_covariate_notes: Covariates are collected at intake by the engine (not by this card). The engine's customer profile aggregates the union of covariates declared by all cards. This card's covariate consumption is light: smoking_status feeds threshold lookup (immune class shows persistent methylation signal from tobacco for years post-cessation; thresholds are calibrated by smoking bin); sex_at_birth is mandatory per CCL-002 because immune-class effect magnitudes differ substantially by sex (VAL-051/057 anchor); HPV status is a Stage 1 stratifier per cerv-LL-002 (not just metadata) because HPV exposure measurably shifts the cervical immune compartment baseline (VAL-074); HIV, transplant_status, and current_treatment_status feed SUPPRESSED-tier interpretation (post-chemo, post-transplant, primary immunodeficiency are real signals per CHK-4.7 / heme-LL-003); prior_cancer_history feeds remission-baseline interpretation; the other covariates are reported back to the customer as context in the report (e.g., 'Note: you reported recent illness within 3 months; immune signals from recent illness can persist for weeks to months'). The covariates are never used by this card to suppress a flag — only to contextualize it in the report.

_runtime_routing_role.run_everything_doctrine: The full SOP chain (Stages 0–10) runs every time, against the IAMAtlas REBUILD posterior only. There is no Xu-538 panel pre-screen and no multi-atlas RUN-everything sweep — those were pre-build patterns retired by the IAMAtlas-only directive.
_runtime_routing_role.lineage_adjacent_discrimination_note: Boundary with progenitor class: CHIP (clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential) presents as a progenitor-class signal but consumes immune-cell production, so apparent immune-fraction shifts must be cross-checked against progenitor A-score. Boundary with secretory class: tumor-microenvironment immune infiltration overlaps the secretory class because TME shifts secretory architectural signal. Both adjacencies are resolved via Stage 4.5 bidirectional decomposition + Stage 8 disease-matrix concordance flags.

stage_2_dual_deconvolution.doctrine: Two mathematically independent deconvolvers run every time. Cross-method confirmation is what Planck used to validate CMB temperature maps (Commander/NILC/SMICA/SEVEM all had to agree); CPG inherits the same discipline. Disagreement between deconvolvers IS diagnostic information — surfaced, not averaged away.

primary_deconvolver.name: Walther IAM Deconvolver
primary_deconvolver.algorithm: Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS) with simplex constraint (Σf=1, f≥0); class-level solve first, then per-cell-type refinement

output_per_patient.per_class_ci: 95% CI propagated from atlas MCMC posterior SDs via Monte Carlo (1000 draws from per-CpG posteriors)
output_per_patient.marker_coverage: fraction of marker substrate observed in patient β

secondary_deconvolver.name: NILC Deconvolver (Needlet Internal Linear Combination)
secondary_deconvolver.algorithm: Generalized least squares with inverse-variance weighting (W=diag(1/σ²)) using per-CpG posterior SDs from the IAMAtlas posterior. No non-negativity constraint imposed during solve; simplex projection applied post-hoc. Mathematically independent from Walther NNLS.
secondary_deconvolver.rationale: Derived from Planck's NILC methodology applied to the methylome. The two deconvolvers are derived from different optimization frameworks (Walther: constrained optimization via NNLS; NILC: variance-weighted least squares). Disagreement reveals β-profile structure neither captures cleanly, surfacing patient-specific peculiarity.
secondary_deconvolver.output_per_patient: Independent per-class fraction estimate + per-CpG residual variance

cross_method_gate.outlier_patient_rule: Any patient with per-class disagreement > 0.20 on >= 2 classes is flagged CROSS_METHOD_DISAGREEMENT; downstream Stage 5+ outputs carry a confidence-reduction flag; the report includes a cross-method-gate warning.

stage_2_dual_deconvolution.stage_2_output: Per-class fractions (8 classes × {walther_f, walther_ci, nilc_f, nilc_ci, agreement_flag}), per-cell-type fractions (115 cells × {f, ci}), cross-method gate verdict

stage_3_foreground_subtraction.doctrine: Empirical foreground subtraction is a SUPPORT tool. The architectural A-score H(β_mean)/H_min IS the physics. When a foreground layer doesn't transfer across cohorts (a real risk for linear-coefficient layers fit on one population), the physics-correct response is to run on raw β and let the architecture speak — not pivot to better regression. Foreground subtraction REDUCES noise from known confounders when it transfers cleanly, never compromises the physics readout.

age_axis_foreground.method: Subtract age-correlated linear-component β shift before downstream A-scoring
age_axis_foreground.transfer_caveat: Layer fit on foundation cohort (female-only EPIC-Italy ages 40–65). Cross-cohort transfer to wider age ranges (e.g. Hannum GSE40279 19–101) requires monitoring; if Δ|r| inverts at runtime, raw-β chain is the fallback.

stage_6_cellular_age.doctrine_recipe_6_3: For each architectural class: compute β_mean = mean of patient's β over that class's marker CpGs. Invert the baseline's (decade → β_mean) curve to find the age at which baseline β_mean equals patient β_mean. That's the per-class cellular age. No training. No regression. The baseline IS the instrument; the patient's β_mean IS the measurement; the cellular age IS the readback.
stage_6_cellular_age.monotonicity_note: β_mean DECREASES with age in healthy reference per Recipe §6.3 line 1900. Patient β_mean above youngest decade → SATURATED_HIGH (assign youngest age). Patient β_mean below oldest decade → SATURATED_LOW.
stage_6_cellular_age.interpretation: The inflammaging quantum. Positive delta = immune system reads older than chronological; negative = younger than chronological.

report_strings.flag_summary_SUPPRESSED: Your immune class score is below your age-matched normal range. Lower than typical can have several meanings — see your immune system health page on the website for context.
report_strings.flag_summary_ELEVATED_aggregate: Your immune class score is mildly elevated compared to your age-matched baseline.
report_strings.flag_summary_ELEVATED_per_cell_type: {n_cell_types} of your immune cell types are showing measurable departure from your age-matched baseline. Specifically: {cell_types_list}.
report_strings.flag_summary_ELEVATED_bidirectional: Your immune cells are showing a mixed pattern — some cell types running higher than typical and others running lower than typical at the same time. This pattern can have several meanings; see the immune system health page for context.
report_strings.flag_summary_SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED_aggr: Your immune class score is significantly elevated compared to your age-matched baseline.
report_strings.flag_summary_SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED_per_: {n_cell_types} of your immune cell types are showing significant departure from your age-matched baseline. Specifically: {cell_types_list}.
report_strings.physician_referral_sentence: We recommend you discuss this finding with your primary care provider.
report_strings._template_slot_note: {n_cell_types} and {cell_types_list} are filled in by the report builder at runtime from the engine's per-cell-type output. cell_types_list is rendered as a comma-separated list with cell types in plain English, e.g., 'CD4 T cells, monocytes, and B cells'.

_strings_design_principle: All flag-summary strings are factual, neutral, and free of disease names. The customer reads what was measured and how it compares to their baseline. The customer does not read interpretation or speculation in the report itself — that lives on the website page linked below. The strings deliberately do not say 'this could mean X' or 'this is associated with Y disease' — those statements are in research publications, reproduced on the website with citations, and are not the engine's role to deliver to a specific customer.

report_vigilance_strings._principle: Vigilance content fires conditionally based on what flagged in the customer's report. The report builder assembles vigilance paragraphs from this lookup based on which cells/classes flagged at which tiers. EDEAR does not specify ages, screening intervals, or specific clinical follow-up tests. All clinical-action language defers to the customer's clinician. EDEAR provides the cellular-level reading; the customer's clinician provides the clinical context. The vigilance content is supportive, not prescriptive.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_NORMAL: Routine monitoring. Continue the lifestyle habits that work for you (sleep, stress management, exercise, the basics that affect immune function). Continue the screening recommendations your clinician has discussed with you. Retest with EDEAR at your standard subscription interval.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_ELEVATED_aggregate: Mild elevation in your immune class score has many possible drivers — recent illness, sustained stress, active allergy season, sleep disruption, lifestyle context. Review whether any of these apply to you over the past few weeks or months. Address what you can address in lifestyle. Continue the screening recommendations your clinician has given you on the schedule they recommended. Retest with EDEAR in 6 months instead of waiting a full year, so trajectory becomes informative — a signal that resolves was your body recovering; a signal that stays or intensifies is more useful information for a clinician conversation.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_ELEVATED_per_cell_type: Mild elevation in {n_cell_types} of your immune cell types ({cell_types_list}) suggests the immune system is responding to something specific. The per-cell pages on the website explain what each elevated cell type does and what research has observed about elevations in each. Review whether any of the common context drivers apply to you — recent illness, sustained stress period, active allergy season, sleep disruption, autoimmune condition. If something fits, addressing it is usually enough. Continue your clinician's recommended screening on the schedule they recommended. Retest with EDEAR in 6 months to see how the signal moves.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_ELEVATED_bidirectional: Your immune cells are showing a mixed pattern — some elevating while others are running lower than typical. This bidirectional pattern is different from a uniform elevation and is worth tracking carefully. The per-cell pages explain what each cell type does and what research has observed about bidirectional patterns. Continue your clinician's recommended screening on the schedule they recommended. We recommend you discuss this finding with your clinician at your next visit and bring this report. Retest with EDEAR in 6 months to track how the pattern evolves.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED_aggrega: Your immune class score is significantly elevated. We recommend you discuss this finding with your clinician. Bring this report — the conversation is more useful with the result in hand than without. Continue your clinician's recommended screening on the schedule they recommend, and ask whether they want to adjust anything in light of the EDEAR finding. Retest with EDEAR every 6 months going forward to track how the signal moves. We do not recommend specific clinical follow-up tests; those are decisions for you and your clinician based on your full health history and clinical context.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED_per_cel: Significant elevation in {n_cell_types} of your immune cell types ({cell_types_list}) warrants a conversation with your clinician. Bring this report. The per-cell pages on the website explain what each elevated cell type does and what research has observed about significant elevations in each. Continue your clinician's recommended screening on the schedule they recommended. Retest with EDEAR every 6 months going forward.
report_vigilance_strings.vigilance_SUPPRESSED: Your immune class score is below your age-matched normal range. SUPPRESSED readings are common when current immunosuppression, active chemotherapy, transplant status, certain biologic medications, or HIV status applies. If you declared one of these contexts at intake, the reading reflects what your body is doing in response to your treatment or condition. If you cannot identify a declared context that explains it, discuss the reading with your clinician at your next visit. Continue your clinician's recommended screening on the schedule they recommended.
report_vigilance_strings._screening_language_rule: EDEAR is not a clinician and does not specify screening tests, ages, intervals, or follow-up workups. All vigilance content uses the phrase 'your clinician's recommended screening' or 'the screening recommendations your clinician has discussed with you' or equivalent — never 'mammography after 40' or 'colonoscopy every 5 years' or any other specific recommendation. The customer's clinician owns the clinical screening conversation; EDEAR provides the cellular reading and supports the clinician conversation.
report_vigilance_strings._per_cell_vigilance_supplement_note: Each per-cell page on the website carries cell-specific vigilance content matching this tier vocabulary. The class-level vigilance content above is the report's class-level paragraph; per-cell findings link to per-cell pages where cell-specific vigilance content (and the cell-specific research observations) live. Engine-side: per-cell vigilance strings live in per-cell card supplements (or in the engine's per-cell lookup table) and are not duplicated in the immune class card.

CPG-VAL-015.what: Aging trajectory — immune cellular age + immune A-score vs chronological age
CPG-VAL-015.cohort: GSE40279 Hannum n=656 healthy whole blood ages 19–101
CPG-VAL-015.anchor: Pre-build VAL-006 sealed r=0.9999 on Hannum (anchor for reproduction)
headline_findings: A_immune vs chronological age: r=-0.197, p=3.69e-07 (Hannum n=656, cross-cohort by construction)
Survived sex stratification (F: r=-0.199 p=2e-4; M: r=-0.210 p=2e-4)
Survived 50/50 CV (|Δr|=0.043, under 0.05 threshold)
Decade-median monotonicity: Spearman ρ=-0.854 (p=0.002)
Class-specific: immune + stem_pluri dominate; cycling/stromal/secretory essentially flat

CPG-VAL-016.title: Cross-disease universal alarm via A_immune
CPG-VAL-016.cohorts: AIBL AD + GSE51057 breast + GSE51032 breast (canonical 115-cell A-scores)
headline_findings: A_immune fires in BOTH AD (d=-0.364, p<0.001) and breast pre-dx (d=+0.688 GSE51057; d=+0.217 GSE51032)
Direction is DISEASE-SPECIFIC: AD hypomethylates, breast hypermethylates
In AIBL, A_immune is the STRONGEST signal (stronger than 7/7 other classes)
In breast cohorts, A_immune is one of several signals (cycling/progenitor outrank it)
Pre-registered Pass-3 (fixed-effect meta) FAILS due to sign-opposition — informative, not adverse
Null test (1000 arm shuffles): observed effect distinguishable from noise (p=0.016)
CPG-VAL-016.note: DIRECTIONAL outcome reflects pre-registration choice. The substantive claim (universal alarm fires across diseases with disease-specific direction) is fully supported. Pass-3 (fixed-effects meta) was the wrong test for sign-heterogeneous effects.

CPG-VAL-017.title: Inflammaging in pooled hull HC
CPG-VAL-017.cohorts: Hannum + Han Chinese + Tsaprouni + GSE51057 HC + GSE51032 HC (n=1,763 pooled)
headline_findings: Pooled A_immune-vs-age r = +0.034 (Pass-1 FAILS) due to cohort-recruitment heterogeneity
General-population cohorts go negative as predicted: Hannum r=-0.197, Han Chinese r=-0.142, Tsaprouni r=-0.056
Case-control HC arms go POSITIVE: GSE51057 r=+0.210, GSE51032 r=+0.061 — survivor selection effect
Late-life acceleration ratio (Pass-3): 2.19 (post-70 slope 2.2x steeper than pre-50, in opposite direction)
Pooled decade-medians show late-life-specific decline (60s peak 0.792, 80s 0.766) — inflammaging signature detected without linear pooled test
Null test confirms pooled regression is washed by cohort heterogeneity (p=1.00 vs cohort-stratified shuffle)
CPG-VAL-017.lessons: Pooled fixed-effects regression is the wrong test when cohorts have heterogeneous recruitment frames. The signal IS detectable in decade-medians + per-cohort breakdown + within-cohort acceleration analysis. Future VAL-017_v2 should use mixed-effects with cohort random effect.
CPG-VAL-017.note: NULL outcome by strict PREREG; substantive late-life-decline signal IS present and Pass-3 IS met. The cohort-heterogeneity finding is itself informative for the card's recruitment-frame guidance.

_open_questions_for_review: Smoking bin definitions: current/0-5/5-15/15+ split is based on the McCarthy 2017 / Joehanes 2016 smoking-EWAS half-life literature. Heath has confirmed 18-years-post-quit (his case) should map to former_smoker_long. Bin boundaries can be tuned with empirical data from the IAMAtlas v1 age-matched cohort once available.

Cell type list: the listed 9 cell types are an intent declaration. Final list depends on which IAMAtlas v1 immune-class cell types have clean enough posteriors to support per-cell-type reporting. Cells without sufficient posterior resolution aggregate up to the immune class.

SUPPRESSED tier handling: immune class running below age-matched baseline can mean immunosuppression, certain medications, post-chemo, post-transplant, HIV+, primary immunodeficiency, cachexia, or late-stage marrow infiltration. The current schema treats SUPPRESSED as a tier with website pointer. Open question: should certain covariates declared at intake (current_treatment_status = active chemo, transplant_status = recent transplant, hiv_status = HIV+, current_immunosuppression = yes) suppress the SUPPRESSED flag (since they explain it) or leave the flag with explanatory context? Current draft leaves the flag with context — the customer is told their score is below baseline AND why their declared context can drive that.

Bidirectional firing tier: current draft fires bidirectional patterns at ELEVATED. Open question: under what conditions should bidirectional fire at SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED instead? The cookbook immune-atlas notes that AD-instance and IBD-instance patterns can have very large directional or per-cell-type magnitudes. A conditional rule (bidirectional with directional |d| > 1.0 fires at SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED) would match the validation evidence; a flat rule keeps the schema simpler.

Tier vocabulary: card uses customer-facing NORMAL / ELEVATED / SIGNIFICANTLY_ELEVATED / SUPPRESSED per wellness-positioning lock-in. Cookbook framework also uses MARGINAL / DETECTABLE / URGENT / FLOOR_BREACH for research-tier reporting. Open question: should the card carry both vocabularies (cookbook tier as engine-internal metadata, customer tier as report-facing label), or stay customer-vocabulary-only and let the cookbook tier live in the cross-reference spec / engine? Current draft is customer-vocabulary-only.
